result:
Both integrate changes from one branch into another. Difference is history shape.

**`git merge`**: joins two branches with a new merge commit. Existing commits unchanged. History shows the real branching. Non-destructive.

**`git rebase`**: replays your commits on top of the target branch. Creates new commits with new hashes. History becomes linear, no merge commit.

```
Before:        A---B---C  main
                    \
                     D---E  feature

merge:         A---B---C---M  main
                    \     /
                     D---E

rebase:        A---B---C---D'---E'  feature
```

Conflicts: merge resolves once. Rebase may ask per replayed commit.

Rebase rewrites history. Do not rebase commits already pushed and shared: others' history diverges, and you need a force push.

Use rebase to tidy local work before sharing. Use merge to integrate shared branches.
